title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (inferred from the notation; the neighbouring pages are unrelated Bourbaki typescript). M is a motive over a number field k_0, and k ⊃ k_0 is a Galois extension. The letters v, w denote embeddings of k into C (complex places). For each v there is an integral Betti realization M_v^Z, the lattice H_B(M ⊗_v C, Z). There is also a fibre functor N_v^Z on the tensor category generated by M, with values in Z-modules. G = G_{M_v^Z} is the corresponding Tannakian (motivic, or Mumford–Tate type) group scheme over Z, possibly over Q.

Comparison of two embeddings. Take two embeddings v, w. Étale cohomology does not depend on the embedding, so M_v^Z ⊗ Z_ℓ ≅ H_et(M, Z_ℓ) ≅ M_w^Z ⊗ Z_ℓ for every ℓ. At infinity, the de Rham comparison gives M_v ⊗ C ≅ H_dR(M) ⊗ C ≅ M_w ⊗ C. 'As usual', this yields an element g of G(A) = ∏_ℓ G(Z_ℓ) × G(C) with M_w^Z = g · M_v^Z. Grothendieck flags the needed hypothesis in a bracketed aside: the two tensor fibre functors N_v^Z and N_w^Z over Z must be isomorphic, i.e. the Isom-torsor between them must be trivial over Z. Granting this, g is determined up to right multiplication g ↦ gh with h ∈ G(Z). A marginal N.B. adds that if one fixes g_∞, the remaining indeterminacy mod G(Z) fixes the ℓ-components g_ℓ.

Galois cocycle. Specialise to w = σv with σ ∈ Gal(k/k_0). One gets M_{σv}^Z = g_σ M_v^Z, which also equals σ_∞ M_v^Z, the transport of structure by σ acting at infinity. A boxed N.B. records the map from complex embeddings of k to those of k_0 (V_k → V_{k_0}): it is surjective, with complex conjugation entering through fibres of cardinality 2. The page ends with a crossed-out box (struck by two diagonal lines) defining a map φ_v : Gal(k/k_0) → G(A)/G(Z) by σ_∞(M_v^Z) = φ_v(σ) M_v^Z.

Meaning. The finite components of φ_v(σ) come from the ℓ-adic Galois representation. The infinite component is a period or de Rham transport. φ_v therefore packages the Galois action and the periods into one adelic class modulo the integral points of the motivic group. Its purpose is to study how the integral Hodge/Betti structure of M changes under conjugation of the embedding, i.e. conjugation of motives.
errors: G(A_ℓ) is written as ∏_ℓ G(Z_ℓ) × G(C). This is an 'integral adele' group, not the usual adelic points (no restricted product over Q_ℓ). It is adequate for comparing lattices but should not be confused with G(A).

The existence of g requires N_v^Z ≅ N_w^Z as tensor functors over Z. A torsor under G over Z need not be trivial. Grothendieck explicitly makes this an assumption, so it is not an error but a genuine gap.

Whether g ↦ gh with h ∈ G(Z) is exactly the indeterminacy depends on G(Z) being the full stabiliser of the lattice structure; this is plausible for G defined as the automorphism group of the integral fibre functor.
The final box defining φ_v is crossed out, suggesting Grothendieck was unsatisfied with the formulation; σ_∞ is not defined precisely on the page.

ideas.what: Comparing Betti lattices of a motive for two complex embeddings via an element of G(∏Z_ℓ × C), using étale and de Rham comparisons
ideas.modern_name: Conjugation of motives / comparison of Betti realizations under Aut(C); adelic torsor between fibre functors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne ('Hodge cycles on abelian varieties', 'Motifs et groupe de Taniyama', LNM 900, 1982); Langlands (1979, conjugation of Shimura varieties); Milne–Shih
ideas.where_published: Not in Grothendieck's published texts as far as I know; the Tannakian framework is in Saavedra Rivano (1972)

ideas.what: Motivic Tannakian group G defined over Z attached to the integral Betti fibre functor; fibre functors for different embeddings assumed isomorphic as tensor functors
ideas.modern_name: Integral motivic Galois / Mumford–Tate group; torsor of tensor isomorphisms between fibre functors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck–Saavedra (over fields); integral versions later (e.g. Deligne, Kisin)

ideas.what: Map φ_v: Gal(k/k_0) → G(A)/G(Z) combining ℓ-adic Galois action and the archimedean period transport
ideas.modern_name: Cocycle underlying the Taniyama group / motivic conjugation (Shimura–Taniyama reciprocity in the CM case)

ideas.what: Map from complex embeddings of k onto those of k_0, with complex conjugation entering through fibres of cardinality 2

missed.claim: Around 1969–72 Grothendieck sets up an adelic invariant φ_v(σ) ∈ G(∏Z_ℓ × C)/G(Z) measuring how the integral Betti structure of a motive changes under conjugation of the complex embedding. This is a prototype of the Langlands/Deligne conjugation formalism behind the Taniyama group and conjugates of Shimura varieties, which appeared about a decade later. Notably, it is formulated integrally (modulo G(Z)) rather than rationally. The thread is abandoned: the defining box is crossed out.
missed.quote: Gal(k/k_0) → φ_v → G(A_ℓ)/G(Z) ... σ_∞(M_v^Z) = φ_v(σ) M_v^Z
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's early anticipation of motivic conjugation and Taniyama-group ideas. The integral version, with a Z-model of the motivic group and the obstruction from non-trivial Z-torsors between fibre functors, is still less developed than the rational theory.

missed.claim: The page treats the isomorphy of integral tensor fibre functors attached to different embeddings as an explicit hypothesis. This implicitly links conjugation of motives to the triviality of torsors under integral motivic groups, a class-number-like obstruction. The theme rarely appears explicitly in the later literature.
missed.quote: on suppose ... que les foncteurs N_v^Z et N_w^Z ... (tensoriels) sont isomorphes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is relevant to integral Hodge/Tate structures and integral canonical models, where torsor triviality over Z is a real issue.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains an early, integral version of the adelic conjugation cocycle for motives (Galois action plus periods in G(Ẑ×C)/G(Z)), predating Langlands–Deligne's Taniyama-group work by roughly a decade. It is sketchy and crossed out, and the rational version is now standard, so it is a notable priority detail rather than a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'G = G_{M_v^Z} est le groupe [?] Q. associé à M, v' — probably 'le gr. sur Z (or sur Q) associé à M, v'; since g is taken mod G(Z), a Z-group is intended.

Bracket reads roughly: '[ici on suppose que les foncteurs fibres N sur N_v^Z et N sur N_w^Z ... multiplicatifs (= tensoriels) ... sont isomorphes ...]'. 'ou L tensoriels' is likely 'ou Z, tensoriels'.
Marginal N.B.: 'si on se fixe g_∞, ce qui fait une indétermination mod G(Z) seulement, tous les g_ℓ sont déterminés'.
Boxed N.B.: 'on aura une surjection non canonique (?) V_k → V_{k_0}, dont les fibres sont ... de card. 2 (conj. complexe)'; uncertain reading.
The final box with φ_v is struck through by two diagonal lines, i.e. crossed out, not merely boxed.
